trial_court: High Court of Meghalaya, Shillong, Crl.Petn. No. 25 of 2023
case_name: Shri. Rahul Kumar Choudhury vs . State Of Meghalaya & Anr.

parties.respondent_defendant: State Of Meghalaya & Anr. (wife and father of minor daughter)

facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent's minor daughter were in a love relationship that ended with the daughter attempting to commit suicide after consuming poisonous substance. Respondent lodged an FIR alleging sexual assault by petitioner.

legal_principles.principle: Courts may give a lenient interpretation to the strict provisions of the POCSO Act if there is an element of consent by the alleged victim.
legal_principles.held: If the case so indicated reveals that there is an element of consent by the alleged victim, the strict provisions of the law may have to be given a lenient interpretation.
cited_cases: Vijayalakshmi & Anr. v. State Rep. By. Inspector of Police, All Women Police Station, Erode: Crl. O.P No. 232 of 2021
use_in: cases involving teenage relationships and consent

legal_principles.principle: Courts may exercise their inherent power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to interfere in a matter when there is an element of ends of justice to be met.
legal_principles.held: This Court, hereby reiterates its respectful agreement with a number of propositions advanced by other High Courts on the subject.
cited_cases: Vijayalakshmi & Anr. v. State Rep. By. Inspector of Police, All Women Police Station, Erode: Crl. O.P No. 232 of 2021
use_in: cases where ends of justice are at stake

outcome.final_order: The court allowed the appeal and set aside the trial court's order.

conducting a judicial proceeding in the High Court of Meghalaya
